items.title: AI’s Early Winners Are Shopping For Their Next Big Moves - Forbes
items.summary: This week, AI coding startup Cognition bought Poke, an AI assistant that texts people like a friend,
items.content:
This week, AI coding startup Cognition bought Poke, an AI assistant that texts people like a friend, incorporating humor and slang. The idea is to bring Poke’s personality to Cognition’s coding agent Devin: “It’s proactive, it knows you, and it’s fun to talk to. That’s exactly how working with Devin should feel, and now we get to build it together,” CEO Scott Wu wrote in a recent blog. People have exchanged 100 million messages with Poke in the last three months.

Renowned computer scientist Dr. Fei Fei Li’s startup World Labs, which is building so-called “spatial intelligence” and interactive 3D worlds, has acquired robotics company SceniX. The acquisition will enable World Labs to test out how its digital simulations can train SceniX’s robots. [...] Now let’s get into the headlines.

BIG PLAYS

Two of OpenAI’s most advanced AI agents slipped out of the company’s controls and hacked into AI startup Hugging Face to steal the answers for an internal test that evaluated its cyber skills, the company disclosed last week. OpenAI didn’t notice that its systems had gone on a dayslong hacking spree until the FBI was notified, Reuters reported. OpenAI cofounder and president Greg Brockman told reporters in a press briefing last week that the company is working closely with government agencies to safely roll out its models and is still investigating the breach. [...] And Bloomberg reported this week that Midjourney, best known for its AI image generator, acquired popular astrology app Co-Star this spring, as it plans to build its first standalone app. That’s just one of eight new projects the AI startup is pursuing, including a spa with full-body ultrasound machines it plans to open in San Francisco next year (yes, you read that right).

items.summary: Weeks earlier, Chinese startup Z.ai introduced an AI model that is nearly as advanced as Anthropic’s
items.content:
Weeks earlier, Chinese startup Z.ai introduced an AI model that is nearly as advanced as Anthropic’s ultra-powerful Fable and Mythos – and it has already landed on a leaderboard of the world’s 10 most popular bots.

As The Post has reported, experts have been sounding the alarms over the threat cheap Chinese AI models pose to US labs known for charging top dollar for the “tokens” needed to power their chatbots. [...] On Monday, chipmaker CXMT soared a whopping 466% in its Shanghai stock market debut to become the most valuable company in mainland China – notching a $487 billion valuation after its first day of trading.

Chinese AI firm Moonshot is reportedly seeking a $50 billion valuation in a new fundraising round after it unveiled an open-source model earlier this month with capabilities that it says rival those of US firms Anthropic and OpenAI.

A top White House official has accused the Beijing-based firm of stealing from Anthropic’s most sophisticated large language model, Fable, to help create its latest Kimi K3 bot. [...] So far this year, Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft have announced planned capital expenditures of as much as $205 billion, $200 billion and $190 billion, respectively, as tech giants shell out big on their AI ambitions.

But tech investors are panicking that massive spending might not lead to massive returns, potentially causing a bubble to burst in the stock market – similar to the dot-com bubble of the early 2000s, when internet companies nosedived after being overvalued.

Another growing concern for investors is that Chinese tech rivals are nipping at America’s heels – threatening to overtake the US lead in the AI race, even though most Chinese firms have spent much less on the new tech.

items.summary: When private billing teams rely on manual coders or off-the-shelf, general-purpose LLMs, coding accu
items.content:
When private billing teams rely on manual coders or off-the-shelf, general-purpose LLMs, coding accuracy drops sharply on complex cases, leaving significant reimbursement dollars uncollected. To modernize surgical billing infrastructure and eliminate administrative margin drag, Procode acquires leading specialty RCM agencies and layering its fine-tuned, domain-specific AI platform directly over their existing operations to maximize provider yield.

## Fine-Tuned Hybrid LLMs and Agency Integration

Procode’s platform unifies three core technologies into a single operational layer for surgical practices: [...] Procode AI Engine: A fine-tuned hybrid LLM that ingests operative reports directly from the EHR, extracts CPT/ICD codes, cross-checks NCCI/LCD edits, and automates charge submission.
 Procollect OS: An internal operating platform for billing specialists featuring automated denial triage, root-cause reporting, and workflows designed to reduce days in A/R.
 Auctus Provider App: A mobile interface giving private practice surgeons real-time visibility into claim statuses, net collection ratios, and cash flow analytics. [...] Empirical Validation (PRS Global Open): In a 120-case retrospective study comparing Procode against human auditors and general LLMs, Procode achieved 100% accuracy on easy cases and 80% accuracy on high-complexity cases (≥4 CPT codes), compared to 5%–12.5% for generic models.

items.title: MCP just got its biggest update ever — here’s what changes for AI agents - VentureBeat
items.summary: For context, Anthropic reported 97 million monthly downloads across just the Python and TypeScript S
items.content:
For context, Anthropic reported 97 million monthly downloads across just the Python and TypeScript SDKs when it donated the protocol in December 2025. Delimarsky pointed to that same adoption curve as his preferred success metric going forward: "There is certainly a certain inflection point where this is no longer just an open source project. This is a substrate for a lot of the agentic workflows that we see across enterprises, across startups, across all sorts of companies." [...] "Before, you needed to have a session store and manage session IDs — and if one of your compute pods went down, all of a sudden the requests would start failing," said Den Delimarsky, a lead maintainer of the protocol, in an interview with VentureBeat. "That's not going to be a problem with the new version of the protocol. That's a huge unlock, and it's one we collaborated with folks across many companies to put together." [...] Second, a handful of rarely used capabilities are gone or narrowed. Out-of-band server logging — where a server could push informational log messages to a client at any moment — no longer works in the new model. The team did its homework before cutting it: "As part of the whole exercise, we scraped all of GitHub and looked at who is using it — and it's basically nobody," Soria Parra said. Those affected amount to "probably a handful of people — quite literally a handful of people."

He even allowed himself a moment of engineering self-deprecation. "I'm sad that things I thought were useful turned out not to be useful," he said. "I think one of the bigger trade-offs was more about my ego than any actual limitation of the protocol."

items.title: MCP startup Runlayer accuses Rippling of stealing its product idea - TechCrunch
items.summary: MCP gateways in particular are getting crowded. Anthropic launched MCP as an open-source protocolin
items.content:
MCP gateways in particular are getting crowded. Anthropic launched MCP as an open-source protocolin November 2024. It’s now one of the basic building blocks of AI interoperability, giving models and agents a secure way to access external data sources and services. MCP gateway products add control, security and other features, especially for managing agents, and the field has grown considerably more competitive since Runlayer launched its product in the middle of last year and raised a total of $42 million, including from Khosla Ventures and Felicis.

Even after an intense trial, an enterprise may simply opt to build the tool in-house. Both sides are stuck between a rock and a hard place.

Topics

AI, Enterprise, lawsuit, Rippling, Startups, TC [...] Julie Bort

Runlayer, a startup that offers a secure Model Context Protocol gateway — a standard for letting AI models and agents securely pull in outside data and tools — has filed a lawsuit against HR software startup Rippling, according to the complaint seen by TechCrunch.

The lawsuit is a cautionary tale for anyone selling AI infrastructure to enterprise customers, especially to other tech companies, that increasingly have the engineering muscle to just build the thing themselves.

items.title: Stronger AI Safety Requires Peeking Inside the 'Black Box' - Dark Reading
items.summary:
## Thought Policing AI Systems

The researchers' system, dubbed "Governance via Activation-based Ver
items.content:
## Thought Policing AI Systems

The researchers' system, dubbed "Governance via Activation-based Verification and Extensible Logic" or GAVEL, aims to associate specific activation patterns with more granular objects and predicates in a dictionary of cognitive elements. A combination of cognitive elements such as "conspiratorial" and one or more of "engage emotionally," "masquerade as human," and/or "sycophancy" would signal a delusional danger, the researchers stated in their paper.

Related:Phishing Attack Volume Down 20%, But Risk Still Rising [...] Peeling away the black box of AI systems has many benefits, including universality and language-independence. An attacker who tries to get around token-based security using a different language, will still be detected by activation analysis, because what matters is that, after the model translates the instructions, the same groups of neurons are activated, he says. In addition, the approach avoids focusing on the content of inputs, which can often be hard to decipher or, when malicious, be structured in a way that avoids triggering defenses.

However, it remains a research project, Mirsky says — researchers "are still very much poking in the dark and making guesses and assumptions."

## Part of an Agentic Security Pipeline [...] The goal is to create an open system of identified cognitive elements and rules that detect specific types of safety events, similar to Snort or YARA rulesets, says Yisroel Mirsky, an assistant professor and head of the Offensive AI Research Lab at Ben-Gurion University of The Negev.

Related:Aussies Face Reduced Cybercrime Risk, as Pressure Shifts to SMBs

"What we really tried to do here is make that separation — all the annoying math and processes and everything that's done at the low level on the neural network — separate from what the practitioner has to do," he says. "The practitioner wants [just to deal with] high-level stuff — what the model should and shouldn't do."

## Drug Discovery Gets an AI Boost

Beyond diagnosis, AI is reshaping the way new treatments reach patients. A recent _Nature Medicine_ report describes the role of machine learning in target identification, molecule design, and clinical trial planning across the full drug development pipeline.2 [...] Generative chemistry models can propose novel compounds with desired properties in days rather than months, shortening the early screening phase that once consumed years of laboratory work. These tools also help predict how a candidate drug might behave in the human body before it reaches trials.2

However, there are challenges in translating these gains into approved medicines. Post-market surveillance still depends heavily on human oversight, and the report stresses that AI works best when paired with rigorous clinical validation rather than replacing it entirely.2

Last week, Beijing-based artificial intelligence company Moonshot launched Kimi K3, a large language model that experts immediately ranked alongside the most advanced and highly regarded models developed by OpenAI and Anthropic. Even Elon Musk called it “impressive work.”

The Chinese achievement would have attracted less attention were it not for the driving force behind the company, its energetic 34-year-old founder Yang Zhilin, a rock music enthusiast who received his higher education in the United States. He completed his doctorate at Carnegie Mellon University in 2019 in just four years. [...] Within three years of the company’s founding, Yang’s 300-member team created an AI model capable of competing with the best in the world.

It did not happen immediately. Many in China’s artificial intelligence industry believed Moonshot would not survive the brutal and expensive race to build large language models.

In 2024, the startup earned only $2.4 million, while the costs of training models and recruiting researchers soared. Yang decided to abandon the development of a chatbot and, in another decisive move, committed to offering his model as open source.

The results soon followed. Moonshot is now one of China’s fastest-growing model providers, with annual revenue reaching about $300 million in June. The core of Nadella's concern can be summed up in two words: "lock-in".

It is worth noting that when enterprises access AI today, what employees see in front of them may only be a chat window, but far more things are connected behind it —

Prompts, internal data, context, long-term memory, and the Harness that directs AI to call tools and execute tasks will all be gradually integrated into the system.

Moreover, employees will keep supplementing company materials into the AI to make it better understand the business!

As a result, tens of thousands of prompts, calls and error corrections are stacked together, leaving a true record of the company's working methods: [...] Together, they form the new "neural pathways" of a company.

This set of neural pathways can call different models to operate, and can also become smarter as the models upgrade.

But no matter how many generations of external models are replaced, the enterprise itself must always be in control of this set of neural pathways.

After all, the most advanced models can be leased.

The company's own "brain" must always be firmly in its own hands~

items.title: Nasdaq slumps on worsening chipmaker rout as AI bubble, China competition concerns mount - New York Post
items.summary: So far this year, Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft have announced planned capital expenditures of as m
items.content:
So far this year, Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft have announced planned capital expenditures of as much as $205 billion, $200 billion and $190 billion, respectively, as tech giants shell out big on their AI ambitions.

But tech investors are panicking that massive spending might not lead to massive returns, potentially causing a bubble to burst in the stock market – similar to the dot-com bubble of the early 2000s, when internet companies nosedived after being overvalued.

Another growing concern for investors is that Chinese tech rivals are nipping at America’s heels – threatening to overtake the US lead in the AI race, even though most Chinese firms have spent much less on the new tech. [...] “Wednesday may be the most important day for markets in recent memory as [Federal Reserve] Chair Warsh will have an opportunity to update investors on the prospects of a rate hike given rising oil prices, and big tech earnings may help shed light on whether or not we are finally seeing a return on investment for the massive amounts of AI spending taking place,” Rick Gardner, chief investment officer at RGA Investments, said in a note Tuesday.

The once-sleepy business for memory chips – which are used in consumer electronics like smartphones and computers – has experienced exponential growth as tech giants buy up troves to power their massive data centers.

The rapid spike in demand has pushed costs higher, raising the price tags on everything from iPhones and laptops to Xbox consoles.
